hints: Read l₁ directly as point plus its given direction vector.
For l₂ use its given point and choose a direction perpendicular to the normal (3,−2,1), satisfying −2y+z=0; write both with separate real parameters.
walkthrough:
Write down the vector equation of line $l_1$ through $(3, 1, -6)$ parallel to $2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = 3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} - 6\mathbf{k} + \lambda(2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k})$$

Find the direction vector $\mathbf{d}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix}$ for line $l_2$ (since it has no $x$-component):
$$\text{Condition: } \mathbf{d}_2 \text{ is perpendicular to } 3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}:$$
$$\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ b \\ c \end{pmatrix} \cdot \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = 0(3) + b(-2) + c(1) = -2b + c = 0 \implies c = 2b$$
$$\text{Choosing } b = 1 \implies c = 2 \implies \mathbf{d}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$$

Write down the vector equation of line $l_2$ passing through $(-1, 3, -6)$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} + \mu\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = -\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} - 6\mathbf{k} + \mu(\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k})$$

hints: Use the scalar-product formula with direction vectors (2,1,4) and (0,1,2).
Divide by their exact magnitudes, take the inverse cosine, and select the acute angle to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Calculate the scalar product of the direction vectors $\mathbf{d}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{d}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\mathbf{d}_1 \cdot \mathbf{d}_2 = (2)(0) + (1)(1) + (4)(2) = 0 + 1 + 8 = 9$$

Apply the cosine formula for the acute angle $\theta$ between the two lines:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{|\mathbf{d}_1 \cdot \mathbf{d}_2|}{|\mathbf{d}_1||\mathbf{d}_2|} = \dfrac{9}{\sqrt{21}\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{9}{\sqrt{105}}$$
$$\sqrt{105} \approx 10.246951 \implies \cos\theta \approx \dfrac{9}{10.246951} \approx 0.878310$$

Evaluate the acute angle $\theta$ to 3 significant figures:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.878310) \approx 28.56^\circ \approx 28.6^\circ \quad (\text{or } 0.498\text{ radians})$$

hints: Equate the three components of general points on l₁ and l₂ using separate parameters.
Solve for both parameters, check all components agree, and substitute back to state the intersection position vector.
walkthrough:
Equate the coordinates of general points on $l_1$ and $l_2$ component by component:
$$x\text{-component: } 3 + 2\lambda = -1$$
$$y\text{-component: } 1 + \lambda = 3 + \mu$$
$$z\text{-component: } -6 + 4\lambda = -6 + 2\mu$$

Calculate the position vector of the point of intersection:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 + 2(-2) \\ 1 + (-2) \\ -6 + 4(-2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ -1 \\ -14 \end{pmatrix} = -\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} - 14\mathbf{k}$$
